predecessors.note: Malik-Shah sent Tutush to Damascus in 1078/9; Atsiz ibn Uvaq had taken it in 1076 (Tutush page). The great-seljuk-empire dossier draws Syria as Seljuk land until its 'split' of November 1092.

successors.note: Damascus: Toghtekin seized the city after Duqaq's death on 6 June 1104 (Ridwan page; Burid dossier).
Aleppo: Ilghazi's takeover ended Seljuk rule (Ridwan page: 1118; the Ilghazi page and the Artuqids dossier: 1117).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. In 1080 Tutush 'took Manbij, Hisn al-Faya, Biza'a, and Azaz to isolate' Aleppo (Tutush page). The page gives no frontier; the belt is drawn as discs round the named places (Hisn al-Faya and Biza'a are approximate).

New keyframe. Aleppo was occupied 'except for the citadel in May 1086' and left in October when Malik-Shah's armies advanced; Malik-Shah appointed Aq Sunqur governor of Aleppo in December 1086 (Tutush page), so the Aleppo belt is dropped. Jerusalem: Tutush 'annexed ... Jerusalem, granting the latter territories to Artuk Bey' (undated; Artuk was made governor of Jerusalem in 1086 per the Artuqids page). The other coastal and Palestinian towns the page lists (Sidon, Gibelacar, Tiberias, Ramla, Jaffa) are undated and not drawn.

New keyframe. Tutush defeated Aq Sunqur and Bozan at Tell Sultan in June-July 1094 and is 'Sultan of Aleppo 1094-1095' (infobox). The 1092-1093 conquest of Nisibin, Amida, Mayyafariqin and Mosul was given up in December 1093 (a hatched occupation in the ledger).

New keyframe. Tutush was killed near Ray on 25 February 1095; Ridwan 'took over the Syrian Seljuk throne' at Aleppo and Duqaq fled to Damascus, 'splitting the Syrian Seljuk state'. Two lines in one dossier: Aleppo (Ridwan, 1095-1113, then Alp Arslan al-Akhras, then Sultan Shah under Lu'lu') and Damascus (Duqaq to 1104).

New keyframe. In 1098 the Fatimid vizier al-Afdal expelled Sökmen and Ilghazi from Jerusalem (Artuqids page). The Crusaders took Antioch in June 1098 and then al-Bara and Ma'arrat al-Nu'man 'and surrounded Aleppo' (Ridwan page); those places are not drawn as Aleppo's before the capture (no page here lists Ridwan's lands).

New keyframe. Duqaq died on 6 June 1104 and Toghtekin took Damascus (Burid dossier); only the Aleppo line is left, under Ridwan (to 10 December 1113), Alp Arslan al-Akhras (killed 1114) and Sultan Shah ibn Ridwan under the regent Lu'lu', until the Artuqid takeover.

ledger.note: 1078: Malik-Shah's brother Tutush takes over Damascus. 'In 1078/9 Malik-Shah sent Tutush to help' Atsiz against a Fatimid siege, after which 'Tutush had Atsiz executed and installed himself in the city'; infobox: Damascus 1078-1095. Atsiz had taken the city in 1076.

ledger.note: 1093: Tutush returns to Syria in December 1093.
1094: Tutush takes Aleppo. He defeated Aq Sunqur and Bozan of Edessa and Harran, who had switched to Berkyaruq, at Tell Sultan in June-July 1094 (both killed); infobox 'Sultan of Aleppo 1094-1095'.

1095: Tutush is killed near Ray on 25 February; Ridwan 'took over the Syrian Seljuk throne' at Aleppo and Duqaq 'fled to Damascus, splitting the Syrian Seljuk state'. The dot moves to Aleppo; the Damascus line (Duqaq, to 1104) stays in this dossier.

1098: the Fatimid vizier al-Afdal Shahanshah expels Sökmen and Ilghazi, the Artuqid governors, from Jerusalem. The fatimid-caliphate dossier records the 1098 retaking of Jerusalem under the counterpart 'Artuqids'.

1104: Duqaq dies on 6 June and Damascus passes to Toghtekin and the Burids. 'Duqaq died of tuberculosis'; Ridwan moved to Damascus and had the sermon read in his own name, though Duqaq's son Tutush II succeeded him (the Burid page: Toghtekin 'seized the city for himself').

1117: Ilghazi takes Aleppo after the assassination of the regent Lu'lu', ending Seljuk rule. The Ridwan page says 'Seljuk rule in Aleppo ended with the Artuqid takeover by Ilghazi' in 1118; the Ilghazi page (cited in the artuqids dossier) gives 1117 and the year is aligned with that gain.
1117: the last Seljuk seat, Aleppo, goes to the Artuqids (page: 1118).

wars.outcome: Tutush defeated Suleiman ibn Qutulmish, who was killed (his son Kilic Arslan captured); no border change recorded.

wars.outcome: Tutush captured Nisibin, Amida, Mayyafariqin and Mosul in 1092-1093 and returned to Syria in December 1093.

wars.name: Battle of Tell Sultan
wars.outcome: Tutush defeated Aq Sunqur and Bozan in June-July 1094 and took Aleppo.

wars.name: War between Ridwan and Duqaq
wars.outcome: Ridwan defeated Duqaq at Qinnasrin on 22 March 1097; the two lines stayed apart (Ridwan page).

wars.name: Ridwan against the Crusaders and Antioch
wars.outcome: Ridwan lost to Bohemond (5 July 1100) and Tancred (Artah, 20 April 1105), gained and lost Apamea (1106), paid tribute to Tancred and, in 1108, ceded two fortresses near Aleppo (Ridwan page).

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Three pages opened; the slug is the one the great-seljuk-empire and artuqids dossiers already use. Wikidata id not obtainable: null (the dossier's 'wikipedia' is the Tutush I article; there is no standalone article for the Syrian Seljuks).
Two lines under one colour: the Damascus line (Tutush 1078-1095, Duqaq 1095-1104; then the Burids) and the Aleppo line (Tutush 1094-1095, Ridwan 1095-1113, Alp Arslan al-Akhras 1113-1114, Sultan Shah under Lu'lu' to 1117). A ruler strip is omitted because two lines run in parallel.
Overlap to settle at the renderer: the great-seljuk-empire dossier carries Syria as Seljuk land and splits off 'Seljuk Syria' in November 1092, while this dossier begins in 1078 (Tutush at Damascus); the 1078-1092 span can be read as an appanage of the Great Seljuks.
Not settled: the Palestinian and coastal towns (Sidon, Gibelacar, Tiberias, Ramla, Jaffa) the Tutush page says were annexed: undated, so only Jerusalem is drawn (placed at 1086, confidence 1); the fatimid-caliphate dossier names 'Artuqids' as the Jerusalem counterpart in 1098, which should be seljuks-of-syria; the Ridwan page says Ridwan 'conquered' Edessa in 1096 and took Turbessel, which the county-of-edessa dossier must settle (not drawn); Ridwan's territory after 1098 (al-Bara, Ma'arrat al-Nu'man, Apamea, Balis) is not listed as a whole on the page; Aleppo ended in 1118 (Ridwan page) or 1117 (Ilghazi page) - 1117 used; the Tutush page's lead gives his Damascus rule as 1078-1092 emir and 1092-1094 sultan, the infobox 1078-1095.
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: 'Mayyafariqin' (and the Hisn al-Faya / Biza'a circle is a coordinate).
